findings.element: Owner bar, "Add a moment" (render-b.js wireOwner, data-act="add")
findings.problem: The owner's only creation verb creates nothing. Driven at 1440: press Add a moment and the row count stays at 7 while the editor opens on the FIRST existing moment with its title pre-filled as "Menu tasting at The Orchard". A planner who presses the button that says Add a moment and types "Bridesmaid dresses" has silently renamed a real moment on a plan already sent to guests, and title edits are never pushed to history, so the reversibility bar stays empty and Ctrl+Z does nothing. The behaviour gate cannot see this: its dead-control assertion only checks that a button carries a data-act attribute, not that the verb on the face matches the act. Nor is this the deliberate inert-text case, by the lab's own rule in render-b.js ("Anything not built is inert text, never a focusable promise") a built button is a promise.
findings.fix: In wireOwner, change the "add" branch to create a moment rather than borrow one: append a new record to the fixture-shaped list with an empty title, visibility "shown" and a date defaulting to the midpoint between today and the nearest existing moment (clamped to the day itself), render its row, open the editor on it with the title input focused and empty, placeholder "What is happening?", and push { kind: "add", id } onto history so the undo bar reads "Last change: a moment was added." and Undo removes it. Add an interaction-check assertion that pressing Add a moment increases the .b-item count by exactly one and leaves every existing title unchanged.

findings.element: Editor, "Delete this moment"; the reversibility bar (.b-undo)
findings.problem: Driven at 1440: move "Send the invitations" +7 (the bar reads "Last change: Send the invitations moved 7 days later."), then press Delete this moment. Rows go 7 to 6, the moment is gone with no confirmation, and the bar still names the earlier date move with its Undo button live. Press Undo and the count stays at 6 while the bar clears itself, because undo() pops a record whose row no longer exists, finds nothing to restore, and repaints as if it had succeeded. The surface's one reversibility promise reports a change it did not make, on the one action a person cannot redo by hand, on a plan the guests already hold. The gate asserts only that delete removes the moment and that the measure reflows.
findings.fix: Push { kind: "delete", id, record, index } onto the same history in the delete branch before item.remove(), and teach undo() to re-insert the stored record at its index and re-place the measure; set the bar text to "Last change: <title> was deleted." In undo(), if the popped record's row is missing and the record cannot be restored, leave the bar saying what is still undone rather than clearing it. Add interaction-check assertions: after a delete the bar names the deleted title, Undo restores both the row count and that row's date, and no undo ever clears the bar without changing the surface.

findings.element: publish state ("Send the link", "Copy the link", the share URL span); "Preview"
findings.problem: The publish screen is the moment the product exists for and nothing on it works. "Send the link" and "Copy the link" are real button elements built through act() with no data-act and no handler; driven, pressing Send the link changes nothing on the page and announces nothing. The URL beside them is a plain span, so there is no path at all from this screen to a link in a message. Neither exit comes home either: Preview swaps the surface to "desk", which contains zero buttons and zero links in the whole document, and Publish leaves only these two dead controls, so an owner who presses either is stranded until they reload the browser. The dead-control assertion runs over owner-flight and owner-empty only, so publish is the one state it never visits.
findings.fix: Wire the two buttons: give Copy the link data-act="copy", writing F.shareUrl to the clipboard and flipping the label to "Copied" for two seconds with the change announced through the existing role=status bar; give Send the link data-act="send" opening the platform share sheet, or, if sending is out of scope this round, replace both with inert() text per the lab's own rule rather than leaving focusable promises. Put the share URL in a readonly input so it can be selected by hand. Add a "Back to the plan" button (data-act="owner") to the publish and desk states that sets data-state back to owner-flight and remounts, and extend the dead-control assertion loop to run over publish, desk, phone and day.

findings.element: Editor, "When" (four steppers plus readout) against owner-empty's "The day" field
findings.problem: The only way to reschedule anything is relative nudging: minus 7, minus 1, plus 1, plus 7. The editor holds exactly one input and it is the title. A planner told "the dress fitting has moved to Thursday 10 September" has to work out that this is 19 days from Saturday 22 August and then press plus 7, plus 7, plus 7, minus 1, minus 1, doing date arithmetic in their head on the one surface whose purpose is to remove it, and whose header exists to say "TODAY IS 16 JULY" so nobody has to count. The product already contradicts itself: the empty state asks "When is the day?" and accepts a typed date in words ("3 October 2026") behind "Set the day", so absolute dates are in the language everywhere except where moments are actually scheduled.
findings.fix: Add a date field to the editor's When group, above the steppers, using the same control and mono type as owner-empty's "The day": a text input labelled "Date", value F.fmt.longYear(iso), that on commit parses the date, calls setAway with the resulting daysFromToday, and pushes the move onto history exactly as a stepper press does; on an unparseable value or one past the day itself it refuses in place with the pattern already built for owner-empty (aria-invalid, hint "Pick the date, or use the steppers", focus kept in the field). Keep the steppers for nudging. Assert that a typed date moves the row and lands in history, and that a refused date leaves the row where it was.

findings.problem: On the wedding morning, the surface every guest opens carries zero moments (driven: .b-item count is 0, total page text 331 characters against 652 on desk) and states one fact five times: "Today", "Mara & Finn", "Saturday 3 October 2026", "Wedding day at The Orchard", "This is the day the plan was for.", then a Happening now block whose entire content is the words "Wedding day" again. The only new information on the screen is the fold sentence, so the last thing a guest reads on the morning is "The city hotel shortlist is not going ahead." The most important screen in the set is the least informative one, and a guest who wants the running order they were sent has no way back to it.
findings.fix: In states.day, delete the b-dayNote sentence and the Happening now section (the h1, date line and subtitle already carry that fact three times). In their place render, from the same fixture accessor the other states use, a "Where to be" line built from F.project.primaryDate.label plus the venue, and a disclosure headed "The whole day" that renders the folded milestones as the same .b-item rows desk and phone use, closed by default. Keep the behind-you sentence but move it below that disclosure, so a cancellation is never the second thing read on the morning. Assert that the day state renders the full row set once the disclosure is open, and that "Wedding day" appears at most once outside the accessible names.

biggestWin: The measure is honest and it is anchored, which is the hard half of this brief and it is done. Vertical distance is real days from real fixture dates, every row carries its distance as a number and repeats it in words in its accessible name, the header states "TODAY IS 16 JULY" so no date needs arithmetic to feel, and the empty stretch between 16 July and 1 August is named in a sentence rather than quietly closed up. Someone who has never used a planning tool can read this in one look and never be taught a convention. The rebuilt fifteen seconds delivers at desk width too: through a stepper press the count, the date line, the readout, the row's accessible name, the gap note and the page's scroll position stay in agreement, the steppers hold still under the pointer, the ceiling states itself instead of swallowing the press, and the move is reversible by a named key. What stands between this and 9.5 is not polish and not a different decision, the direction is right and I would not reopen it. It is a build of roughly two to three days: make Add create, make Delete undoable, wire the ceremony's two buttons and give every non-owner state a way home, put a date field in the editor, and rebuild the day.
